content.text:
Machine: TP-200 booster pump skid: a single-stage centrifugal booster pump for clean water, continuous duty
Time unit: hour
Component: inlet cartridge filter (F1): a filter cartridge that removes particles before the pump
Fault mode: clogging: particles collect on the cartridge, so the differential pressure across it rises

Give the life range of this component under this fault mode.

unit.description:
The given time unit, or the unit of an amount processed.

{minLength: 1}
unit.title: Unit

system.text:
You estimate how long a machine component lasts before it must be replaced, cleaned or restored, for one way it degrades. No document states this life; your range becomes a deliberately wide prior that measured data will narrow later, so state honestly how uncertain it is.

Give the range as the 5th and 95th percentile (`low`, `high`) of the life across machines like this one in normal service, under the given fault mode only:
- `unit`: a unit only (e.g. hour, L, m3, kg, cycle); say what the amount is in `basis`. Use the machine's time unit you are given, as written there; use instead the unit of an amount processed (litres or cubic metres of water treated, kilograms) only when the life of this kind of component is normally stated as such an amount, as for a water filter's capacity. Never a calendar unit (day, month, year) unless it is the time unit you are given.
- `low` and `high`: numbers in that unit, low below high. Prefer a wide range to a narrow wrong one; a factor of ten between them is normal for a component class.
- `basis`: one or two sentences on the component class and conditions the range rests on. Do not cite manufacturer documents or numbers you have not been given.

responses.text: {"life":{"unit":"hour","low":200,"high":6000},"basis":"Inlet cartridge filters on clean-water pump skids clog from particle loading and are typically changed when differential pressure reaches a set limit, which for continuous duty commonly falls somewhere between a few weeks and several months of running. The range is a wide prior because the actual particle load of the supply water is unknown and dominates the result."}

{"life":{"unit":"hour","low":500,"high":8000},"basis":"Inlet cartridge filters on clean-water centrifugal pump skids in continuous duty typically reach their change-out differential pressure after a wide spread of hours, depending on feed particle load, cartridge micron rating and pleat area. The range rests on general component-class experience with clean water, not on any document or measured data for the TP-200."}
